build_inputs.angles:
- It went round Laguna Seca in one minute twenty-eight point six five, a production car record. The same driver, back to back, managed a twenty-nine eight nine in a Porsche 918 and a thirty seven one in a McLaren P1.
- Both of those are hybrids. This is 645 horsepower and 600 lb-ft from an eight-point-four litre V10 with no turbos and no electric motor anywhere.
- It took the production car lap record at thirteen North American tracks, and Dodge's own vehicle dynamics engineer set eleven of them himself.
- The aero package makes over seventeen hundred pounds of downforce at its top speed, which is also why its top speed is only 177.
- It cost about 18,000 new and a good one is worth roughly 50,000 today -- it went UP. Never say it depreciated.

script: Setting a blazing lap time of one minute twenty-eight point six five at Laguna Seca, this monster beat the hybrid Porsche 918 and McLaren P1. That record-breaker is the 2016 Dodge Viper ACR, an icon of raw performance and engineering prowess. The Viper's aluminum X-brace improves chassis rigidity, a crucial feature for handling tight curves under pressure. With 645 hp and 600 lb-ft of torque, its 8.4-liter V10 delivers explosive power through a manual six-speed transmission. Dominating tracks with over 1,700 pounds of downforce, the Viper ACR excels in both speed and cornering capabilities. Originally priced at about $120,000, it's a bargain given its track pedigree and rare performance. The red Viper logo on the steering wheel signifies its racing heritage, a nod to enthusiasts. So, is a track beast without hybrid gimmicks your style, or would you opt for electric assists?

sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 2016 Dodge Viper ACR, finished in Viper White with a black interior. This Viper's odometer currently displays approximately 9,200 miles. The attached Carfax vehicle history report shows no accidents or mileage discrepancies in this Dodge's past. It also confirms that this Viper has been registered in Florida and Texas since new. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, notable factory equipment includes 19-inch ACR wheels, an aluminum structural X-brace, a limited-slip differential, manually adjustable coilover suspension, leather and Alcantara upholstery, Sabelt bucket seats, and a Uconnect infotainment system with an 8.4-inch touchscreen display. Notable modifications reported by the seller include aftermarket 3-inch headers and exhaust system, an Arrow Racing Engines Stage 1 PCM tune, slotted brake rotors, and a Schroth racing harness for the driver's seat. The fifth-generation VX I Viper launched in 2013 and replaced the fourth-generation ZB II Viper, which finished production in 2010. Launched under the SRT brand, the fifth-generation Viper was unveiled at the 2012 New York International Auto Show. The performance-oriented ACR is positioned near the top of the Viper lineup, just below the track-focused ACR Extreme. Power comes from an 8.4-liter V10, rated at 645 horsepower and 600 lb-ft of torque in stock form. Due to the modifications performed to this Viper, it may produce more power, but a dyno sheet was not provided to confirm. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 6-speed manual transmission.
